mcqs.q: Which three landmarks are marked on the casts before the arrangement begins?
opts: The midline, the crest of the ridge and the midpoint of the retromolar pad
The midline, the incisive papilla and the hamular notch
The crest of the ridge, the vibrating line and the retromolar pad
The midline, the fovea palatinae and the buccal shelf
mcqs.explain: The casts are marked indicating midline, crest of the ridge, and the midpoint of the retromolar pad.

mcqs.q: What is the stated purpose of marking these cast landmarks?
opts: They will be used to check the arrangement
They indicate where the denture border will finish
They locate the posterior palatal seal
They establish the vertical dimension of occlusion
mcqs.explain: The landmarks are marked because they will be used to check the arrangement.

mcqs.q: Mounting is defined as:
opts: The laboratory procedure of attaching a cast to an articulator
The clinical procedure of recording jaw relations
The laboratory procedure of investing a denture in a flask
The clinical procedure of seating a trial denture
mcqs.explain: Mounting is the laboratory procedure of attaching a cast to an articulator.

mcqs.q: In the visit 3 workflow, anterior teeth arrangement is classified as:
opts: A laboratory procedure
A clinical procedure
Part of the jaw relation record
Part of teeth selection
mcqs.explain: Teeth arrangement — anterior then posterior — is a laboratory procedure, following transfer of the jaw relations to the articulator.

mcqs.q: For the maxillary central incisor, where should the MESIAL of each tooth lie?
opts: On the midline
On the inner edge of the land
Over the incisive papilla
8 mm forward of the papilla
mcqs.explain: The mesial of each central incisor should be on the midline.

mcqs.q: The incisal edge of the maxillary central incisor should be:
opts: Parallel to and in contact with the occlusal plane
½ to 1 mm above the occlusal plane
½ to 1 mm below the occlusal plane
Touching the plane at its tip only
mcqs.explain: The central incisal edge should be parallel to and in contact with the occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: Viewed from the facial aspect, the long axis of the maxillary central incisor shows:
opts: A slight mesial inclination to the perpendicular
A slight distal inclination to the perpendicular
No inclination — it is exactly perpendicular
A pronounced distal inclination
mcqs.explain: From the facial aspect, the long axis shows a slight mesial inclination to the perpendicular.

mcqs.q: Viewed in profile, the cervical aspect of the maxillary central incisor should be:
opts: Slightly depressed
Slightly prominent
In line with the incisal edge
Set forward of the incisal edge
mcqs.explain: In profile the cervical aspect of the tooth should be slightly depressed.

mcqs.q: The maxillary lateral incisor is usually positioned at what level relative to the plane of occlusion?
opts: ½ to 1 mm above it
½ to 1 mm below it
In contact with it
2 mm above it
mcqs.explain: The lateral incisor is usually ½ to 1 mm above the plane of occlusion.

mcqs.q: The maxillary lateral incisor is positioned with:
opts: A slight mesial inclination
A slight distal inclination
No inclination
A marked labial inclination
mcqs.explain: It is positioned with a slight mesial inclination, in relationship with the central incisor.

mcqs.q: Which maxillary anterior tooth is the one NOT in contact with the occlusal plane?
opts: The lateral incisor
The central incisor
The cuspid
All three are clear of the plane
mcqs.explain: The central incisal edge is in contact with the plane and the cuspid tip touches it; only the lateral incisor is lifted ½ to 1 mm above it.

mcqs.q: Viewed from the occlusal, the incisors should follow:
opts: The curvature of the internal aspect of the land
The outer edge of the land
The line of the ridge crest
A straight line through the incisive papilla
mcqs.explain: From the occlusal, the incisors follow the curvature of the internal aspect of the land.

mcqs.q: Viewed in profile, the incisal tip of the maxillary cuspid should:
opts: Touch the occlusal plane
Sit 1 mm above the occlusal plane
Sit 1 mm below the occlusal plane
Sit level with the lateral incisor edge
mcqs.explain: In profile the cuspid has a slight mesial inclination from the perpendicular and the incisal tip touches the occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: In the 'toed-in' position of the cuspid, how are the cervical and incisal edges related?
opts: They are aligned vertically
The cervical edge is set well forward of the incisal
The incisal edge is set well forward of the cervical
They diverge towards the distal
mcqs.explain: The cervical and incisal edges of the cuspid are aligned vertically, while the facial surface is canted inward.

mcqs.q: What causes the facial surface of the cuspid to appear 'toed in'?
opts: The prominence of the cervical area of the tooth
The mesial inclination of its long axis
Its contact with the lateral incisor
The curvature of the inner edge of the land
mcqs.explain: The facial surface is canted inward and appears toed in due to the prominence of the cervical area of the tooth.

mcqs.q: The cuspid has two planes on its labial surface. Viewed from the anterior, which should be visible?
opts: Only the mesial plane
Only the distal plane
Both equally
Neither — the surface should appear flat
mcqs.explain: The cuspid has a mesial plane and a distal plane on the labial surface; from the anterior only the mesial plane should be visible.

mcqs.q: A student can clearly see the distal plane of the set cuspid when looking from the front. What does this indicate?
opts: The cuspid has not been turned in far enough
The cuspid has been rotated in too far
The cuspid is set too high above the occlusal plane
The cuspid has excessive mesial inclination
mcqs.explain: Only the mesial plane should be visible from the anterior, so a visible distal plane means the toed-in position has not been achieved.

mcqs.q: Using the incisive papilla as a biometric guide, the central incisor lies:
opts: 8–10 mm anterior to the incisive papilla
8–10 mm posterior to the incisive papilla
4–6 mm anterior to the incisive papilla
Directly over the incisive papilla
mcqs.explain: The central incisor is 8–10 mm anterior to the incisive papilla.

mcqs.q: Using the incisive papilla as a biometric guide, the canine lies:
opts: Perpendicular to the incisive papilla in the sagittal plane
8–10 mm anterior to the incisive papilla
Perpendicular to the incisive papilla in the frontal plane
At the junction of the papilla and the midline
mcqs.explain: The canine is perpendicular to the incisive papilla in the sagittal plane.

mcqs.q: Why is the incisive papilla a useful guide in an edentulous patient?
opts: It is a stable landmark that does not resorb with the ridge
It marks the position of the posterior palatal seal
It moves forward with the ridge as resorption proceeds
It indicates the vertical dimension of rest
mcqs.explain: The papilla is stable and does not resorb with the ridge, so it can be trusted to place teeth when the natural teeth are long gone.

mcqs.q: Horizontal overlap (overjet) is defined as:
opts: The projection of teeth beyond their antagonists in the horizontal plane
The distance teeth lap over their antagonists as measured vertically
The angle between the incisal edges in protrusion
The space between the incisal edges in centric occlusion
mcqs.explain: Horizontal overlap / overjet is the projection of teeth beyond their antagonists in the horizontal plane.

mcqs.q: Vertical overlap (overbite) is defined as:
opts: The distance teeth lap over their antagonists as measured vertically
The projection of teeth beyond their antagonists in the horizontal plane
The vertical dimension of occlusion minus the rest dimension
The vertical distance from the incisal edge to the occlusal plane
mcqs.explain: Vertical overlap / overbite is the distance teeth lap over their antagonists as measured vertically.

mcqs.q: The recommended vertical overlap at this stage is:
opts: 2 mm
3–4 mm
0 mm — the edges should meet
mcqs.explain: Vertical overlap 0.5–1 mm; horizontal overlap 2 mm.

mcqs.q: The recommended horizontal overlap at this stage is:
opts: 2 mm
4 mm
It is left to the operator's judgement
mcqs.explain: Horizontal overlap should be about 2 mm.

mcqs.q: The purposes of horizontal and vertical overlap are:
opts: Esthetics, phonetics and function of balance in protrusion
Esthetics, retention and stability
Phonetics, retention and support
Esthetics, support and resistance to lateral force
mcqs.explain: The purpose is esthetics, phonetics and function of balance in protrusion.

mcqs.q: The horizontal overlap should be:
opts: Consistent throughout the anterior region
Greatest at the centrals and least at the cuspids
Least at the centrals and greatest at the cuspids
Measured only at the central incisors
mcqs.explain: The horizontal overlap should be consistent throughout the anterior region, about 2 mm at this stage.

mcqs.q: The mandibular central incisors are set with their long axis:
opts: Perpendicular to the occlusal plane, with the neck depressed
Perpendicular to the occlusal plane, with the neck prominent
With a slight mesial inclination and the neck depressed
With a slight distal inclination and the neck prominent
mcqs.explain: The mandibular central incisors are set with the long axis perpendicular to the occlusal plane with the neck depressed.

mcqs.q: The mandibular lateral incisors are set with:
opts: A slight mesial inclination
A long axis perpendicular to the occlusal plane
A slight distal inclination
More mesial inclination than the canines
mcqs.explain: The mandibular lateral incisors are set with a slight mesial inclination.

mcqs.q: Compared with the mandibular lateral incisors, the mandibular canines have:
opts: More mesial inclination, with the neck set prominently
Less mesial inclination, with the neck depressed
The same inclination but a depressed neck
No inclination at all
mcqs.explain: The mandibular canines have more mesial inclination than the lateral incisors and the neck is set prominently.

mcqs.q: Which anterior tooth is set with its long axis PERPENDICULAR to the occlusal plane?
opts: The mandibular central incisor
The maxillary central incisor
The maxillary cuspid
The mandibular canine
mcqs.explain: The mandibular central is the one anterior tooth set perpendicular; every other anterior tooth carries some mesial inclination.

mcqs.q: Regarding the neck position, which pairing is correct?
opts: Mandibular central — neck depressed; mandibular canine — neck prominent
Mandibular central — neck prominent; mandibular canine — neck depressed
Both are set with the neck depressed
Both are set with the neck prominent
mcqs.explain: The mandibular central incisor is set with the neck depressed, while the mandibular canine's neck is set prominently.

mcqs.q: Incisal guidance is defined as:
opts: The influences of the contacting surfaces of the guide pin and guide table on articulator movements
The influence of the anterior teeth on mandibular movement in the patient
The angle formed between the incisal edges in protrusion
The inclination of the incisal guide table in degrees
mcqs.explain: Incisal guidance is the influences of the contacting surfaces of the guide pin and guide table on articulator movements.

mcqs.q: The two components named in the definition of incisal guidance are the:
opts: Guide pin and guide table
Condylar element and fossa assembly
Maxillary and mandibular incisors
Occlusal plane and the land area
mcqs.explain: The definition refers specifically to the contacting surfaces of the guide pin and the guide table on the articulator.

mcqs.q: The adjustable incisal guide table can be set over what range?
opts: 0 degrees to 20 degrees
0 degrees to 30 degrees
10 degrees to 40 degrees
0 degrees to 60 degrees
mcqs.explain: The adjustable incisal guide table is adjustable from 0 degrees to 20 degrees.

mcqs.q: In denture construction, the relationship of the mandibular incisors to the maxillary incisors in centric occlusion should be that they:
opts: Never touch
Touch lightly and evenly
Touch only at the central incisors
Touch with 0.5 mm of vertical overlap
mcqs.explain: In denture construction the mandibular incisors should NEVER touch the maxillary incisors in centric occlusion.

mcqs.q: The incisal guide angle in denture construction should be kept:
opts: As low as possible
As high as possible
Exactly at 20 degrees
Equal to the horizontal condylar inclination
mcqs.explain: It should be kept as low as possible, to enhance free movement of the teeth in protrusive and lateral excursions.

mcqs.q: Why should the incisal guide angle be kept as low as possible?
opts: To enhance free movement of the teeth in protrusive and lateral excursions
To increase the vertical overlap for esthetics
To allow the mandibular incisors to contact in centric
To reduce the horizontal overlap below 2 mm
mcqs.explain: A low incisal guide angle enhances free movement of the teeth in protrusive and lateral excursions.

mcqs.q: Why are the anterior overlaps deliberately kept small in a complete denture?
opts: So the anterior teeth do not contact in centric or lock during excursion and tip the base
So the denture can be made with non-anatomic posterior teeth
To reduce the amount of acrylic needed in the labial flange
To allow the incisive papilla to be used as a guide
mcqs.explain: Anterior contact in a complete denture tips the base and unseats it, so the overlaps are kept small (0.5–1 mm vertical, 2 mm horizontal) and the guide angle low.

mcqs.q: Why is the midpoint of the retromolar pad marked ON THE LAND of the cast rather than on the pad itself?
opts: The pad is covered once the teeth are set, but the mark on the land stays visible
The pad is too soft to take a pencil mark
The land mark is needed to orient the face bow
The pad position changes during mounting
mcqs.explain: A mark carried out onto the land remains readable after the teeth cover the pad region.

mcqs.q: A set-up is checked and the central incisor labial surface is found 5 mm anterior to the incisive papilla. What does this indicate?
opts: The centrals are set too far palatally
The centrals are set too far labially
The papilla has been marked in the wrong place
The arrangement is correct
mcqs.explain: The central incisor should lie 8–10 mm anterior to the incisive papilla, so 5 mm means it has been set too far back.

saqs.q: Which landmarks are marked on the casts before arranging the anterior teeth, and why?
saqs.a: MARK THE CASTS indicating the MIDLINE, the CREST OF THE RIDGE and the MIDPOINT OF THE RETROMOLAR PAD; these landmarks are used to CHECK THE ARRANGEMENT. On the maxilla the INCISIVE PAPILLA, the MIDLINE and the ANTERIOR LAND AREA are identified; on the mandible, the RIDGE CREST lines and a mark on the LAND indicating the midpoint of the retromolar pad.

ans.text: The casts are marked with the midline, the crest of the ridge and the midpoint of the retromolar pad — these landmarks are used to check the arrangement.

MANDIBLE

the ridge crest lines · a mark on the land indicating the midpoint of the retromolar pad

saqs.a: THE LABORATORY PROCEDURE OF ATTACHING A CAST TO AN ARTICULATOR.

ans.text: The laboratory procedure of attaching a cast to an articulator.

saqs.q: Describe the position of the maxillary central incisor in all three views.
saqs.a: FRONTAL — the MESIAL of each tooth should be ON THE MIDLINE and the INCISAL EDGE PARALLEL TO AND IN CONTACT WITH THE OCCLUSAL PLANE. FACIAL — the LONG AXIS shows a SLIGHT MESIAL INCLINATION to the perpendicular. PROFILE — the CERVICAL ASPECT should be SLIGHTLY DEPRESSED, judged against the inner edge of the land and the occlusal plane.

head: View
Position
rows: the mesial of each tooth on the midline, and the incisal edge parallel to and in contact with the occlusal plane
the long axis shows a slight mesial inclination to the perpendicular
the cervical aspect slightly depressed — judged against the inner edge of the land and the occlusal plane

saqs.q: Describe the position of the maxillary lateral incisor.
saqs.a: It is positioned with a SLIGHT MESIAL INCLINATION and is usually ½ TO 1 mm ABOVE THE PLANE OF OCCLUSION. In profile the slight mesial inclination is seen in relationship with the central incisor, and again the tooth is slightly above the plane.

rows: a slight mesial inclination — seen in profile in relationship with the central incisor
usually ½ to 1 mm ABOVE the plane of occlusion

saqs.q: How do the incisors relate to the land when viewed from the occlusal?
saqs.a: THE INCISORS FOLLOW THE CURVATURE OF THE INTERNAL ASPECT OF THE LAND. This is what the anterior land area was marked for — it gives a drawn curve to set the arch form against instead of judging it by eye.

ans.text: The incisors follow the curvature of the internal aspect of the land. This is what the anterior land area was marked for — it gives a drawn curve to set the arch form against, instead of judging it by eye.

saqs.q: Describe the position of the maxillary cuspid in profile.
saqs.a: The cuspid has a SLIGHT MESIAL INCLINATION FROM THE PERPENDICULAR, and THE INCISAL TIP TOUCHES THE OCCLUSAL PLANE.

ans.text: A slight mesial inclination from the perpendicular, with the incisal tip touching the occlusal plane.

saqs.q: Explain the 'toed-in' position of the cuspid.
saqs.a: The CERVICAL AND INCISAL EDGES of the cuspid are ALIGNED VERTICALLY. The FACIAL SURFACE, however, IS CANTED INWARD and appears TOED IN, DUE TO THE PROMINENCE OF THE CERVICAL AREA. Two different things are being described — the tooth's vertical alignment and the orientation of its facial surface — and the cervical bulge is what turns the face inward while the edges stay in line.

head: What is aligned
What is canted
rows: the cervical and incisal EDGES are aligned vertically
the FACIAL SURFACE is canted inward and appears toed in, due to the prominence of the cervical area

ans.text: Two different things are being described — the tooth's vertical alignment and the orientation of its facial surface. The cervical bulge is what turns the face inward while the edges stay in line.

saqs.q: What are the two planes on the labial surface of the cuspid, and how are they used as a check?
saqs.a: A MESIAL PLANE and a DISTAL PLANE. WHEN VIEWED FROM THE ANTERIOR, ONLY THE MESIAL PLANE SHOULD BE VISIBLE. This is the practical test of the toed-in position: if the distal plane can be seen from the front, the cuspid has not been rotated in far enough.

head: The two planes
The check
rows: a MESIAL plane and a DISTAL plane on the labial surface
viewed from the anterior, only the mesial plane should be visible

ans.text: This is the practical test of the toed-in position — if the distal plane can be seen from the front, the cuspid has not been rotated in far enough.

saqs.q: State the two relationships that use the incisive papilla as a biometric guide, and say why the papilla is suitable.
saqs.a: The CENTRAL INCISOR is 8–10 mm ANTERIOR TO THE INCISIVE PAPILLA. The CANINE is PERPENDICULAR TO THE INCISIVE PAPILLA IN THE SAGITTAL PLANE. The papilla is suitable because it is a STABLE landmark that does not resorb with the ridge, so it can be trusted to place teeth in an edentulous mouth.

ans.text: The papilla is suitable because it is a stable landmark that does not resorb with the ridge — so it can be trusted to place teeth in an edentulous mouth.

saqs.q: Define horizontal overlap and vertical overlap, and give the value of each.
saqs.a: HORIZONTAL OVERLAP (overjet) is the PROJECTION OF TEETH BEYOND THEIR ANTAGONISTS IN THE HORIZONTAL PLANE — about 2 mm. VERTICAL OVERLAP (overbite) is the DISTANCE TEETH LAP OVER THEIR ANTAGONISTS MEASURED VERTICALLY — 0.5–1 mm.

head: Definition
Value
rows: the projection of teeth beyond their antagonists in the horizontal plane
the distance teeth lap over their antagonists, measured vertically

saqs.q: What are the purposes of horizontal and vertical overlap?
saqs.a: ESTHETICS, PHONETICS and FUNCTION OF BALANCE IN PROTRUSION. A flat edge-to-edge relationship does not look natural; the F, V and S sounds depend on the anterior relationship; and the overlaps must be proportioned so the anterior teeth do not lock and tip the denture during protrusive movement.

head: Purpose
Why
rows: a flat edge-to-edge relationship does not look natural
the F, V and S sounds depend on the anterior relationship
the overlaps must be proportioned so the anterior teeth do not lock and tip the denture during protrusive movement

saqs.q: Describe the arrangement of the mandibular anterior teeth.
saqs.a: The MANDIBULAR CENTRAL INCISORS are set with the LONG AXIS PERPENDICULAR TO THE OCCLUSAL PLANE with the NECK DEPRESSED. The MANDIBULAR LATERAL INCISORS have a SLIGHT MESIAL INCLINATION. The MANDIBULAR CANINES have MORE MESIAL INCLINATION THAN THE LATERAL INCISORS and the NECK IS SET PROMINENTLY. The inclination therefore increases as you move back from the midline.

head: Tooth
Arrangement
rows: long axis perpendicular to the occlusal plane, with the neck depressed
more mesial inclination than the lateral incisors, with the neck set prominently

ans.text: The inclination therefore increases as you move back from the midline.

saqs.a: THE INFLUENCES OF THE CONTACTING SURFACES OF THE GUIDE PIN AND GUIDE TABLE ON ARTICULATOR MOVEMENTS. Note that the definition concerns the ARTICULATOR — the guide pin and guide table — not the patient's own teeth; it is the mechanical counterpart of the anterior guidance in the mouth.

ans.text: The influences of the contacting surfaces of the guide pin and guide table on articulator movements.
Note that the definition concerns the articulator — the guide pin and guide table — not the patient's own teeth. It is the mechanical counterpart of the anterior guidance in the mouth.

saqs.q: Over what range is the adjustable incisal guide table set?
saqs.a: From 0 DEGREES TO 20 DEGREES, the adjustments being made at the table itself, which can be tipped to match the guidance the case requires.

ans.text: From 0° to 20° — the adjustments being made at the table itself, which can be tipped to match the guidance the case requires.

saqs.q: State the rule governing the anterior teeth in denture construction, and explain why it exists.
saqs.a: In denture construction, THE MANDIBULAR INCISORS SHOULD NEVER TOUCH THE MAXILLARY INCISORS IN CENTRIC OCCLUSION, and THE INCISAL GUIDE ANGLE SHOULD BE KEPT AS LOW AS POSSIBLE, TO ENHANCE FREE MOVEMENT in protrusive and lateral excursions. The reason is that anterior contact in a complete denture TIPS THE BASE AND UNSEATS IT — which is also why the overlaps are kept small at 0.5–1 mm vertical and 2 mm horizontal.

list: The mandibular incisors should NEVER touch the maxillary incisors in centric occlusion
The incisal guide angle should be kept as LOW as possible, to enhance free movement of the teeth in protrusive and lateral excursions

ans.text: The reason is that anterior contact in a complete denture tips the base and unseats it — which is also why the overlaps are kept small, at 0.5–1 mm vertical and 2 mm horizontal.

saqs.q: Summarise how each anterior tooth relates to the occlusal plane in the maxilla.
saqs.a: CENTRAL INCISOR — incisal edge PARALLEL TO AND IN CONTACT WITH the plane. LATERAL INCISOR — ½ to 1 mm ABOVE the plane. CUSPID — incisal TIP TOUCHING the plane. All three carry a slight mesial inclination.

head: Tooth
Relation to the occlusal plane
rows: incisal edge parallel to and in contact with the plane

ans.text: All three carry a slight mesial inclination.

saqs.q: Where does anterior teeth arrangement sit in the sequence of visit 3?
saqs.a: Visit 3 begins with the CLINICAL procedures — JAW RELATIONS (horizontal, vertical and orientation relations, the last by FACE BOW RECORD) and TEETH SELECTION. The LABORATORY then TRANSFERS THE JAW RELATIONS TO THE ARTICULATOR, carries out TEETH ARRANGEMENT — ANTERIOR teeth first, then POSTERIOR — and finishes with WAXING & CARVING.
